claims.text: Ethiopia and Eritrea broke diplomatic ties on October 1, 2026, after accusing each other of stoking internal conflicts.
Eritrea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced on Thursday that it was severing all diplomatic ties with Ethiopia in response to the expulsion of its diplomats from Addis Ababa.
Ethiopia declared 10 Eritrean diplomats in Addis Ababa, including the charge d'affaires and diplomats accredited to the African Union, persona non grata and ordered them to leave within 48 hours.
Ethiopia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs accused Eritrea, Sudan, and Egypt of supporting an opposition alliance led by the Tigray People's Liberation Front.
Ethiopia annexed Eritrea in 1962, and Eritrea secured independence in 1993 following an armed struggle led by President Isaias Afwerki.
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed moved to normalise diplomatic relations with Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki when Abiy came to power in 2018.
The 2022 Pretoria Peace Agreement ended a two-year civil war between the Ethiopian federal government and the Tigray People's Liberation Front.

An opposition coalition against Ethiopia's federal government includes the Tigray People's Liberation Front, the Oromo Liberation Army, a faction of the Ogaden National Liberation Front, and militant groups from Benishangul-Gumuz and Afar.
A medic in the southern Tigrayan town of Alamata reported that 52 civilians died during three days of heavy fighting.
An African Union mediator estimated that 600,000 lives were lost during the civil war in Ethiopia between 2020 and 2022.
Eritrea's Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel denied that Eritrea was backing the newly formed rebel alliance fighting the Ethiopian government.
Ethiopia's National Intelligence and Security Service announced an indefinite ban on drone flights in Addis Ababa and surrounding areas.
French police arrested 1,949 people and reported 305 police officers injured during nationwide high school protests on Thursday.
France's interior ministry reported that 1,027 out of 3,700 high schools across the country were affected by student actions, including blockades at 222 schools.
University students in France joined the high school demonstrations on Thursday, blocking access to about 30 university campuses.
Regional prefect authorities in Strasbourg ordered tram services to halt after protesting students placed barriers on the tracks.
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu held a crisis meeting on Thursday to address escalating student unrest across the country.
A bin fire at the Nelson Mandela high school in Nantes spread to the front of the building and damaged the entrance hall.
The headteacher at Degrugillier high school in Auchel sustained an ear injury from a firework during student protests.
French National Rally leader Marine Le Pen called for a new anti-rioting law, stating that the protests were "riots organized by professionals and overseen by deputies from La France Insoumise."
Protesters outside Saint-Exupery high school in Marseille forced firefighters to flee their vehicle before setting the fire truck on fire.
French Education Minister Édouard Geffray scheduled meetings for Friday with representative staff unions, parent groups, and student associations.
The French government announced that many high schools would switch to online classes due to safety concerns from ongoing student protests.
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez launched an internal police investigation following allegations of excessive force and brutality against three students.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged European partners on social media to immediately release strategic diesel reserves to address supply disruptions.
Average US diesel prices surged over 70 percent to $6.39 per gallon following the start of the US war on Iran, according to AAA data.
US President Donald Trump stated he was considering a potential ban on US diesel exports to curb domestic fuel costs.
French President Emmanuel Macron planned a video meeting of G7 leaders for mid-October to discuss coordinating releases of fuel reserves.
European Union trade chief Maros Sefcovic warned that any US ban on diesel exports would be "unexpected for Europeans" and cause "very dramatic consequences" for economic performance.
British ministers held calls on Thursday with counterparts from the European Commission, Germany, France, Italy, and Ireland to discuss drawing down emergency diesel reserves.
The average price of a litre of diesel in the United Kingdom reached a record high of 199.72p on Wednesday, according to the RAC.
Brent crude oil prices rose above $101 per barrel on Thursday, up from about $72 a barrel in February prior to the Iran war.
PetroChina cancelled October shipments of gasoline and jet fuel to destinations beyond Hong Kong and Macau to protect domestic supplies.
Russia extended its export ban on diesel for fuel producers through October 31 to maintain domestic fuel market stability.
Global trade intelligence firm Kpler reported that crude exports from the Gulf region reached 16.5 million barrels per day in September, returning to pre-war averages excluding Iran.
Kpler recorded that refined product shipments through the Strait of Hormuz averaged 677,000 barrels per day in late September, down from 3.6 million barrels per day before the Iran war.
Three Liberian-flagged oil tankers were struck by projectiles on Tuesday while transiting the Strait of Hormuz.
